vintage: 2017; Panel Study of Income Dynamics, 1980 to 2013
table: Table 4, Model 2: Logit models of out-mobility from origin tract
title: Spring, Ackert, Crowder and South, 'Influence of Proximity to Kin on Residential Mobility and Destination Choice: Examining Local Movers in Metropolitan Areas', Demography 54(4):1277-1304
universe: PSID household heads, non-Latino Black or White, who stayed in the same metropolitan area across each interval: 103,276 person-periods from 13,897 persons, 16,545 of them a move to a new census tract
limits: Out-mobility is leaving the census tract for another tract in the same metro area, not leaving the county or town. Kin count as nearby within 1 mile of the origin tract (tract centroids). Each odds ratio is for having at least one relative of that type nearby, with individual and tract controls; the model does not count relatives one by one. Standard errors are those printed with the odds ratios.

oddsRatios.textQuote: Having a parent within 1 mile of the origin tract reduces the odds of out-mobility by 47 %
